title: Depression
hookLine: the Church encourages getting help; grace works through doctors too
tomorrow: Jesus said don't worry. so is anxiety a sin?

cards: Months of gray. Sleep doesn't fix it. Food tastes like nothing.
Prayer, if you pray, feels like talking into a pillow. Is that a spiritual test, or an illness? Inside the Church, people answer in two ways, and each side has a saint or a scripture behind it.

teach.b: The first voice says: this could be the soul's winter. Saint John of the Cross wrote of a dark night, when prayer goes dry and God seems gone, and saw it as a way God draws a person closer.

Their best case: not every sorrow is a disorder, and faith has words for darkness that a chart doesn't. The second voice says: this could be an illness, and illness needs a doctor. Their case is old too.
Ecclesiasticus, in the Douay-Rheims: "Honour the physician for the need thou hast of him: for the most High hath created him."
And: "The most High hath created medicines out of the earth, and a wise man will not abhor them." Where the two meet is a story.
The prophet Elijah lies down under a tree and asks to die. God's first answer isn't a lecture. An angel touches him and tells him to get up and eat.
Bread, water, sleep. One to tell a friend: the angel comes back a second time, because the road ahead is too long for him. You don't have to pick a side.
A spiritual director and a doctor can work the same case, and grace can walk through a counselor's door.

teach.h: HELP IS HOLY. 988 IN THE US.
teach.b: If anyone is in danger or thinking of self-harm, call or text 988 in the US, or your local emergency number, right now.

how: Catholics are encouraged to seek medical and psychological care alongside prayer, the sacraments and spiritual direction; in danger or a crisis, call or text 988 in the US or local emergency help.

o: a punishment for not praying often enough
a short bad mood after a disappointing day
a heavy, lasting low that can need medical care

games.q: two voices, one story — tap the pairs.

s: the Church treats depression as proof of weak faith
scripture honors the physician, and grace can work through doctors and counselors.
God's first answer to Elijah under the tree was food and sleep
an angel touched him and told him to get up and eat, and came back a second time.
Ecclesiasticus tells the sick to avoid medicine and trust God alone
the most High hath created medicines out of the earth, and the wise don't despise them.

games.q: your aunt says your cousin's long low is spiritual dryness and he should pray more. you think he needs a doctor. to be fair to her, what's her side's best case?
o: faith has words for darkness, like the dark night, that a chart doesn't.
doctors can't help with anything that touches the soul.
depression is caused by a lack of faith, so prayer alone fixes it.
games.why: her best point is that faith knows dark seasons. and Ecclesiasticus honors the physician: both can work the same case. in danger, 988.

practice: Make a quiet plan, for yourself or for someone you're worried about. Who's one person to tell: a parent, a counselor, a doctor, a friend? What might get in the way?
And what's the first small step, one message or one call? If you pray, you can ask for the courage to take it.

wordCard.voice: Depression. A heavy, lasting low that can need a doctor as well as prayer, and is no sign of weak faith. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: physician. the word the Latin Bible uses in Ecclesiasticus 38, honor the physician.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: help is holy, whether it comes as bread, a doctor, or a friend. Go gently.
